To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a new, rapid and accurate diagnostic test (multiplex PCR assay) for VAP in patients with suspected VAP is associated with a significant reduction in antibiotic exposure and antibiotic costs without an increase in mortality or in the number of patients who do not receive appropriate antibiotic treatment.
the use of an antimicrobial stewardship program in the ICU can be effective in reducing the incidence of multidrug-resistant organisms and in improving the appropriateness of antimicrobial use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of compounds, the 1,4-dioxane-2,5-diones, as potential anti-cancer drugs.
the development of a novel approach to the design of a new class of antibiotics.
the study of the mechanisms of bacterial resistance to antibiotics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence supporting the current recommendations for empiric treatment of VAP is insufficient to guide clinical practice.
the current evidence does not support the routine use of selective decontamination of the digestive tract in critically ill patients.
the current evidence does not support the use of either the 4-g or the 2-g dose of ceftazidime for empiric treatment of VAP.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the epidemiology of ventilator-associated pneumonia has changed over the last two decades and that the choice of empirical antibiotic therapy must reflect this change.

the current guidelines for empiric antibiotic treatment of ventilator-associated pneumonia are inadequate and need to be revised.
